items.question: What is the difference between LangVersion and Target Framework Moniker?
items.answer: LangVersion tells Roslyn which C# syntax is legal — records, collection expressions, etc. TFM like net10.0 selects which Base Class Library APIs exist in reference assemblies. You can use older TFM with newer LangVersion only if you do not call APIs that do not exist. Upgrading TFM fixes API breaks; raising LangVersion adopts syntax. Pin both in Directory.Build.props for consistent CI.

items.sixtySeconds: LangVersion syntax. TFM APIs. Upgrade TFM first. Pin in central props.

items.question: Name three C# 9–11 features and where you used them in this curriculum.
items.answer: Records for immutable DTOs module 05. Nullable reference types for honest APIs module 07. Init-only properties and required members module 04. Pattern matching switch expressions module 11. IAsyncEnumerable streaming module 13. Collection expressions module 08. Tie each to a scenario — order DTO, auth branching, SQS paging.

items.question: How do you split domain, DTO, and persistence models?
items.answer: Domain enforces rules — Order.Ship validates lines. DTO is wire shape — OrderDto for JSON and Redis without behavior. EF entity is persistence — map to domain or DTO at repository boundary, not in controllers. On hot CSV import use record struct rows before optional promotion to class DTO. Map once per request, not domain to DTO to view model chains.
followUps: When is exposing EF entity from minimal API acceptable?
How does Result<T> fit at the boundary?
items.sixtySeconds: Domain behavior inside. DTO at edge. Map once. struct row for bulk import.

items.question: What do you flag first in a senior code review of an SQS consumer?
items.answer: Correctness and cancellation: is CancellationToken passed through receive and database calls? Then sync-over-async — .Result or .Wait. Then concurrency — shared Dictionary without Concurrent prefix. Then allocations — ToList or string concat per message. Then API surface if library code. SkiaSharp or streams without using. Name the fix from the relevant module.
followUps: How do you handle poison messages?
items.sixtySeconds: Cancellation first. No Result. Concurrent collections. No alloc loop. using native.

items.question: Walk through the expanded six-step code-review radar.
items.answer: One: security and correctness — auth, validation, poison messages, no secrets in logs. Two: async — no Result, CancellationToken through stack. Three: concurrency — no lock across await, ConcurrentDictionary or channels. Four: memory — no ToList per message, span parse, using on native. Five: API and nullability — public types intentional, no null! without proof. Six: performance claims need BenchmarkDotNet or dotnet-counters evidence.
items.sixtySeconds: Six steps: security, async, concurrency, memory, API, measured perf. Correctness before style.

items.question: How do you prove idiomatic span parsing is faster than Split?
items.answer: BenchmarkDotNet with MemoryDiagnoser on a representative CSV line fixture — baseline string.Split versus ReadOnlySpan walk plus TryParse. Report gen-0 allocations per operation, not just nanoseconds. Idiomatic C# without measurement fails senior review. dotnet-counters on staging after deploy validates production gen-0 drop. Same discipline as proving ValueTask on a sync-complete cache path.
items.sixtySeconds: BenchmarkDotNet MemoryDiagnoser. Split baseline versus span. gen-0 per op. Staging counters confirm.

items.question: When is record struct better than class DTO on import?
items.answer: Million-row CSV hot path — record struct CsvRow avoids heap allocation per line when paired with span field parsing. class OrderDto remains fine for HTTP and Redis boundaries where few instances exist. Domain class holds behavior. EF entity never crosses the API. Benchmark class versus record struct row in a parse loop before choosing.
items.sixtySeconds: record struct millions of rows. class DTO at API. Domain behavior. EF inside repo only.

items.question: Your library ships with LangVersion latest — what breaks for consumers?
items.answer: Consumers on older SDKs cannot compile against syntax they do not understand — pin LangVersion to the minimum your team supports and document required SDK in README. latest on a NuGet is a breaking change for downstream rebuilds. TFM still controls API availability — LangVersion 14 on netstandard2.0 compiles until you call a net10-only API. ApiCompat catches public surface breaks; LangVersion pin catches syntax surprises.
items.sixtySeconds: latest hurts consumers. Pin LangVersion. Document SDK. TFM separate. ApiCompat on public API.
